description: Two-panel TEM figure of the Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 high-entropy steel powder milled for 35 h. (a) is a bright-field TEM micrograph of the milled powder: an essentially featureless, mottled grey image with no resolvable grain boundaries or second-phase particles, only faint nanometre-scale fluctuations in diffraction contrast; a white scale bar in the lower-right corner is labelled "20 nm". (b) is the corresponding selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern, rendered as a split image: the left half shows the dark-field pattern with a bright central beam and continuous concentric Debye–Scherrer rings, while the right half carries three blue dashed annotations reading "BCC(110)", "BCC(200)" and "BCC(211)" against the rings; a bright wedge-shaped beam-stop shadow occupies the centre-right of the pattern, and a white scale bar in the lower-right corner is labelled "10 1/nm". Read together, the two panels make one argument: the contrast on the 20 nm scale in (a) is consistent with a nanocrystalline powder obtained after 35 h of milling, and the continuous, non-spotty rings in (b) demonstrate a randomly oriented, polycrystalline BCC structure whose three strongest reflections are (110), (200) and (211). No grain size, d-spacing or lattice parameter is printed on either panel; the caption states the ring pattern corresponds to the BCC phase.

subfigures.description: TEM bright-field micrograph of the 35 h milled high-entropy steel powder, showing uniform mottled grey contrast without resolvable grain boundaries or precipitates; white scale bar labelled '20 nm' in the lower-right corner.

Selected area electron diffraction pattern of the same sample, shown as a split image: left half is the dark-field pattern with a bright central beam and continuous concentric rings; right half is annotated with blue dashed markers labelled 'BCC(110)', 'BCC(200)' and 'BCC(211)'. Bright wedge-shaped beam-stop shadow near the centre; white scale bar labelled '10 1/nm'.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a TEM bright-field image with an identifiable white scale bar reading '20 nm' in the lower-right corner.
Panel (a) shows mottled, low-contrast grey structure with no resolvable grain boundaries, second phase or lattice fringes at the supplied resolution.
Panel (b) is a selected area electron diffraction pattern showing a bright central beam surrounded by continuous concentric rings rather than discrete spots.
Panel (b) carries printed annotations 'BCC(110)', 'BCC(200)' and 'BCC(211)' on blue dashed lines marking the ring positions.
Panel (b) has a reciprocal-space scale bar reading '10 1/nm' in the lower-right corner.
Panel (b) is displayed as a split image with a bright wedge-shaped beam-stop shadow occupying the centre-right region of the pattern.
The caption states that (a) is the TEM bright-field image of the 35 h milled sample and (b) is its corresponding selected area diffraction pattern.
The caption states that the polycrystalline ring pattern corresponds to the BCC phase.
The citing text states that nanocrystalline grains were formed after 35 h of milling.
The citing text states that the ring diffraction pattern corresponds to the BCC crystal structure with planes (110), (200) and (211) identifiable from the rings.
The citing text states that the ring pattern represents the polycrystalline nature of the alloy.
Neither panel prints any numeric grain size, d-spacing or lattice parameter; only the two scale bars carry numbers.

measured_quantities: nanocrystalline grain size (nm, referenced to the 20 nm scale bar)
reciprocal-space ring positions (1/nm, referenced to the 10 1/nm scale bar)
unreadable_items: no grain-size value or interplanar d-spacing is printed on either panel, so the nanocrystalline grain size cannot be read from the figure
individual grains cannot be delineated in panel (a) at the supplied resolution
